note: Set-ups pres-harbour-steps and pres-dim-lighthouse written to the plan's premises (follow-ups in chains-president). Rations used: goose 1 (pres-quiet-harbour-goose); no biscuits, statue or exclamation mark. No new names.

papers.text: Dim the lighthouse at night. A sign on it: HUSH, FISH SLEEPING.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: The hat parade would like kite day. Hats fly too, briefly.
papers.subject: hats

papers.text: Let us hire the Guild's roof. A bus is 12 % more bus from above.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: A practice hut by the anglers, labelled SOUNDPROOF (MOSTLY).
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: Present the Quiet Competition cup. Rodney will hold up your speech.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: Your face on the new stamp. Mildred has seen three, and kept one.
papers.subject: portraits

papers.text: An inquiry: is a kite in the harbour a fish? The League objects.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The kite-or-fish inquiry wants a second summer. The kite is undecided.

papers.text: Fly the founding napkin as a kite. It has been folded for this.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: Give us the spotters' holiday. They spend 80 % of it at our windows.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: Register every hedge: name, age, and any kite it is holding.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: Sit for the new coin. A bus sits for the back, not the shop bell.
papers.subject: portraits

papers.text: A marquee for our show. Then over the bus stop. Then the bus.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: A study of ripples in Saltpenny Bay. So far, 40 % are the band's.
papers.subject: harbours
papers.biggerStudy: The ripple study would now like the waves. Ewan has a second pencil.

papers.text: Hat stands along the harbour, each labelled: HATS. NOT KITES.
papers.subject: hats

papers.text: Lend our prize onion the hat in the Guild's window. Then the gloves.
papers.subject: hats

papers.text: We will hire the harbour as a display. The sea must keep still.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: Give the League the bus's front seat. Kites fly 30 % higher from it.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: We will hire the Quiet Competition's interval. Then the rest of it.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: Open the hedge show. The ribbon is a hedge; shears provided.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: We will hire the bandstand for the onion parade. Wave as they pass.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: A working group: is a kite on a hat a hat? The hats think not.
papers.subject: hats
papers.biggerStudy: The group now studies the reverse. A hat has been seen flying.

papers.text: The band asks for the harbour steps. The anglers may keep the wet ones.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: Pin the first-prize rosette on the onion. Rodney has one for you.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: A committee to date the new holiday. It may only meet on holidays.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The holiday committee needs more holidays to meet on. Three, to start.

papers.text: Carry the bass drum in the parade. It photographs better unplayed.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: A hat with a smaller hat on it. The smaller hat has a request.
papers.subject: hats

favour.text: The smaller hat asks for a place in the kite festival. It will need a string.

clippings.sign: PRESIDENT FLIES HAT AT KITE FESTIVAL; KITES UNIMPRESSED
clippings.refuse: HAT REQUEST FILED FOR FURTHER STUDY

papers.text: We will hire the harbour on the holiday. It is 88 % quiet, 12 % goose.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: A kite museum. The hedge outside holds most of the exhibits.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: Hedge day and kite day clash. Ours was filed first, in triplicate.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: A willow on the quay to sit under. The Committee may admire it.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: A ceremony to honour your ceremonies. Rodney has booked you.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: A rain gauge for the next holiday. No reason. It hopes to be useful.
papers.subject: picnic-weather

favour.text: About the rain gauge: it would like the front row at the show.

clippings.sign: PRESIDENT GIVES RAIN GAUGE FRONT ROW; GROWERS STAND
clippings.refuse: RAIN GAUGE STAYS ON DESK, HOPEFUL

papers.text: A fanfare for every ribbon you cut. Scissors up on the last note.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: A study: do vegetables like brass? So far, the leeks lean towards it.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The leek study now wants the runner beans. They have begun to lean.

papers.text: A plaque where the harbour bus turns. Footnotes on the shop.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Be our window display for an hour. Your card: PRESIDENT, ONE ONLY.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: Clip the bus stop hedge into a bus. Then a queue. Then a late one.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: Make your birthday a national holiday. Mildred has a drawer for these.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: A committee on hedge manners. May a spotter lean on one? Draft due.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The manners committee wants a second volume: bowing to topiary.

papers.text: Give us the band's holiday. We will observe it, in silence.
papers.subject: ceremonies
